1.he: אבל אין מעמידים פסולי כהנה (סנהדרין ל"ב.)
1.note: Reference kept as printed; the rule that judges must be of lineage fit to marry into the priesthood stands in Sanhedrin 36b (Mishnah 4:2).

2.note: Folio read as כ"ו (26a) from the print; the seven good men of the town are discussed in Megillah 26a-27a.

3.he: אין זה עוד ראיה כי אין די לדון דיני ממון
3.note: Elliptic; read as: the name 'court of seven' does not prove that three are too few for monetary cases.

4.he: ויהודה בן בבא התנדב בכל יום אשם תלוי
4.note: Name kept as printed; the Mishnah (Keritot 6:3) tells this of Bava ben Buta.

5.note: Reference kept as printed; the Mishnah stands in Keritot 25a.

6.note: Isaak Markus Jost, the historian; the name only is given.

7.note: Read as from בדים, 'lies': 'we are liars'. The printed form is unusual.

8.note: The print reads ל"ז (37a); Rabban Gamaliel's enactment on witnesses' signatures is at Gittin 36a. Kept as printed.

9.note: Bikkurim has only three chapters in standard editions (ch. 4 is an appended baraita). Kept as printed.

10.note: The abbreviation can stand for R. Judah or R. Yose; R. Judah ha-Kohen is the likely reading.

11.note: Printed כ"ו. (26a); the mishnah is Ketubot 2:9, on 27a-b in the Bavli. Kept as printed.

12.note: Read as 'to winnow and to purify' (להבר from ברר), as printed.

13.note: Print unclear (OCR ותששבתי); read ותשובתי, 'and my reply'.

14.note: Abbreviation kept; probably Abraham Epstein, author of Mi-Qadmoniyyot ha-Yehudim (1887).

15.note: ב"ה is ambiguous: Beit ha-Midrash, or Beit Talmud, where the article named in the note on p. 186 appeared.

16.note: Reference kept as printed; the baraita on Helene's candelabrum stands in Yoma 37b.
